scope: Every comparison in metrics/by_metric/cfm_*.json that rests on a cohort labelled real / reference / baseline / band / literature. For each, what that cohort ACTUALLY is, read from the script that produced it. No new experiments; every number below is recomputed from a file on disk or read from one.
question_per_metric: is there a comparison, and is the thing being compared against actually what it is labelled as?

verdict_legend.SOUND: the reference is what it is labelled as, the protocol matches on both sides, and both sides went through the same code path.
verdict_legend.PROVENANCE-UNVERIFIED: the reference is plausibly real but the producing script / cohort could not be traced to a source dataset on disk, or the label cannot be confirmed.
verdict_legend.CIRCULAR: the reference side is the model's own output (decoder, reconstruction, or the same pipeline), so the comparison measures the generator against itself.
verdict_legend.ASYMMETRIC: the two sides were produced by different code paths, different checkpoints, different protocols, or different populations. The comparison is uninterpretable regardless of the numbers.
verdict_legend.SOUND_WITH_CAVEAT: the reference is what it is labelled as and the protocol matches, but a confound named in the source file (size, population, seed spread) limits the claim to the narrow reading. Cite with the caveat.

the_two_known_instances_reconfirmed_inde: BLK-C-L4 (real_tmqm_reference.csv is decoder output) -- RE-CONFIRMED by direct read of the file, not by citing the prior audit. 636/636 rows carry bracket-atom notation; row 1 is 'CC(C)P(C(C)C)[C](C)(C)[Os]([Br])([Br])...'. No reference corpus carries [C]/[Rh] notation.

BLK-C-L5 (metal-deletion control) -- REPRODUCED exactly. The production sampler (random.Random(0xF00D).sample over the 31152 six-metal rows of .data/molmetal/tmQM/tmqm_parsed.csv) gives 380/600 = 0.6333, matching the recorded value to 4 dp, and the generated side gives 54/66 = 0.8182 under the pinned embedder. This one is sound.
the_three_new_ones: SINGLE-FRAGMENT RATIO: the 0.8365 'real corpus' band is a decoder artefact. Measured on 600 REAL tmQM molecules drawn by the same seeded sampler, single_fragment_ratio is 0.9983, not 0.8365. The generated cohort's 0.9697 is therefore WORSE than the real corpus, not better. The claim 'the model produces MORE connected structures than the real corpus' inverts.

CHEMISTRY VALIDITY / VALENCE: the panel's own valence_ok scores 636/636 on the decoder band and 66/66 on generated, but 29/600 = 0.0483 on real tmQM, while RDKit's own SanitizeMol passes 600/600. The evaluator's _sum_valence adds |charge| for ANIONS and nothing for CATIONS, so every cation (ammonium N+ at valence 4 vs allowed [3]) is a false violation. 99.0% of real tmQM molecules carry a cation; 0.0% of the decoder band and 0.0% of the generated cohort do. The evaluator is blind to exactly the population the reference corpus is made of.

METAL COORDINATION CAP: metal_coord_ok is 441/600 = 0.7350 on real tmQM against 66/66 and 636/636 on the two model cohorts. The shipped caps (Pt 5, Ru 7, Ir 6, Rh 6, Os 7, Re 8, derived from bo_sum p99) are exceeded by real DFT structures, worst overshoot 4 bond orders (Rh, Ru). No control was ever run on real data, so 'no metal centre exceeds its MEASURED cap' was measured only on molecules our own decoder produced.

rows.claim: logPapp -3.0387 generated vs -3.0794 'real'; logS -8.0099 vs -8.3385
rows.what_the_reference_really_is: decoder output

The gap between the two cohorts is 0.04 log units, far inside what a heuristic's clamp can produce. These are NOT independent measurements of two cohorts; they are two evaluations of one formula.

systemic_findings.the_dominant_error_class_is_still_the_sa: The number was not wrong; the CLAIM about the number was. Two of today's nine instances (BLK-C-L4, BLK-C-L5) were this audit's own prior work, which means the error class has a 2-for-2 hit rate on this line and should be assumed present wherever a reference label appears.
systemic_findings.why_it_keeps_happening: Every instance traces to the same mechanism: a control cohort was built by running the system's own output through part of the system. real_tmqm_reference.csv is decoder output. The 'generated' arms of the NCI-60 and single-fragment-QED measurements are reconstructions. The valence and metal-cap checks were only ever run on decoder output. The cheapest available cohort is always the one the pipeline already produces, and it is almost never the corpus.
systemic_findings.the_cheapest_structural_fix: Any cohort used as a reference must come from a path that does not call the model's decoder. Three such cohorts already exist and are cheap: .data/molmetal/tmQM/tmqm_parsed.csv (100849 rows with SMILES, 31152 on the six train metals), molmetal/data/nci60_precious_9cell.csv, and .data/molmetal/tmQM/tmqm_parsed.csv coordinates directly for geometry. This audit's real-tmQM control over 600 molecules runs on CPU in well under a minute.
systemic_findings.scorers_that_are_not_measurements: AMES, logPapp and logS are closed-form heuristics (metrics_v2.py:304, :229, :402 -- Benigni-Richard SMARTS, Hou 2007 linear form, Delaney 2004 ESOL). SA is RDKit-Contrib Ertl sascorer, the only implementation available in this venv; mordred exposes no SA descriptor among its 1613 and openbabel 3.1.0 computes none. QED is RDKit's. Verified this session. So every panel comparison against a literature value is a comparison between our single implementation and another group's single implementation, with no way to tell an implementation difference from a method difference.
systemic_findings.charges_are_the_unexamined_axis: 99.0% of real tmQM molecules on the six train metals carry a formal cation and 98.3% an anion -- tmQM writes dative bonds as charge-separated [O+]#[C-]->[Re+]. 0.0% of the decoder band and 0.0% of the generated cohort carry either. Every chemistry-validity evaluator in this record is charge-asymmetric: _sum_valence adds |charge| for anions and nothing for cations, so a cationic ammonium N is flagged as 5-valent nitrogen. This single asymmetry explains CFM-07 and CFM-08 at once and is worth a fix before any chemistry-validity number is quoted again.
systemic_findings.what_is_definitely_still_standing: The bond-perception record (CFM-01 to CFM-03) and the geometry-collapse record (CFM-15, CFM-16, CFM-30) use real, controlled, like-for-like references and survive this audit intact. They are also, conveniently, the two findings that do not depend on any reference band at all.

audit_method.enumeration: All 29 metrics/by_metric/cfm_*.json were read. Files with no comparison against a real/reference/baseline/band/literature cohort (cfm_run_census, cfm_bond_accuracy, cfm_soft_valence_scale, cfm_assemble_hinge_tau, cfm_l5_metal_deletion_control, cfm_embed_failure_localisation, cfm_generated_geometry_defect, cfm_l3_guidance_ab, cfm_vina_generated as a whole) contributed rows only where they contain a comparison.
audit_method.provenance_resolution: For every cohort labelled real/reference/baseline, the producing path was traced by grep, not by reading the metric file's own description. Where the metric file's self-description and the code disagreed, the code won.
audit_method.controls_run: CPU-only recomputation of the panel (SA / QED / single_fragment_ratio) and of the chemistry-validity sub-flags on a 600-molecule real tmQM cohort drawn by the SAME seeded sampler the L5 control uses, so it is directly comparable to the recorded 0.6333 embed rate.
